title: Plutonium Half-Life Decay
learningObjectives: Define half-life as the time to lose half of radioactivity.
Compare isotopes with different half-life values measured in years.
Calculate remaining amount after elapsed time for isotopes that decay more quickly or slowly.

evidence.quote: The different isotopes have different “half-lives” – the time it takes to lose half of its radioactivity.

explanations.text: Half-life is the time it takes to lose half of radioactivity, and different isotopes have different half-lives.

evidence.quote: Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241’s half-life is 14.4 years.

explanations.text: Plutonium isotopes have specific half-life values, such as 24,100 years for Pu-239 and 14.4 years for Pu-241.

evidence.quote: Substances with shorter half-lives decay more quickly than those with longer half-lives, so they emit more energetic radioactivity.

explanations.text: Substances with shorter half-lives decay more quickly than those with longer half-lives and emit more energetic radioactivity.

predictions.prompt: Start with 100 grams with a 10-year half-life. How much remains after 20 years?
